units.title: Reading and Writing: Information and Ideas

outcomes.text: Work out the central idea of a text.
Interpret the key details that support the central idea.
Pick the fact, detail or example from a text that best backs a stated claim.
Pick the data in a table or graph that best backs a stated claim.
Draw reasonable conclusions from what a text states outright or only implies.

units.title: Reading and Writing: Craft and Structure

outcomes.text: Work out the meaning of a useful academic word or phrase from its context.
Choose the word or phrase that fits a passage's meaning and tone.
Analyze how a text is organized.
Identify the main rhetorical purpose of a text.
Draw reasonable connections between two texts on related topics.

units.title: Reading and Writing: Expression of Ideas

outcomes.text: Combine information and ideas on a topic into one effective sentence that meets a stated aim.
Choose the transition word or phrase that logically links ideas in a text.

units.title: Reading and Writing: Standard English Conventions

outcomes.text: Use punctuation correctly to mark the end of a sentence.
Punctuate clauses, series, appositives and parentheticals within a sentence, and spot where no punctuation is needed.
Make a subject and its verb agree in number.
Make a pronoun and its antecedent agree in number.
Use verbs and verbals (gerunds, participles, infinitives) appropriately in context.
Choose suitable verb tenses and aspects.
Place modifying elements such as participles sensibly in a sentence.
Choose among singular, plural and possessive nouns and pronouns, and among its/it's, their/they're/there, your/you're.
Create and use linear equations in one variable to solve problems in many contexts.
Identify or build a one-variable linear equation that matches a context.
Interpret a constant, variable, factor, term or solution of a linear equation in context.
Solve a one-variable linear equation, using algebraic structure strategically.
Tell when a one-variable linear equation has no, one or infinitely many solutions.
Solve one-variable linear equations fluently.
Create and use linear functions to solve problems in many contexts.
Identify or build a linear function that models a relationship between two quantities.
Interpret an input/output pair, constant, variable, factor or term of a contextual linear function.
Interpret the graph of a linear function in context.
Connect the table, algebraic form and graph of a linear function outside a context.
Connect the table, algebraic form and graph of a linear function in context.
Given an input find the output (or the reverse) for a contextual linear function and interpret it.
Write a linear function's rule from two input/output pairs or one pair and the rate of change.
Evaluate a linear function for an input, or find the input for a given output.
Create and use linear equations in two variables to solve problems in many contexts.
Identify or build a two-variable linear equation modelling a constraint on two quantities.
Interpret a solution, constant, variable, factor or term of a two-variable linear equation in context.
Interpret the graph of Ax + By = C in context.
Connect algebraic forms and graphs of two-variable linear equations outside context.
Connect tables with algebraic forms or graphs of two-variable linear equations outside context.
Connect tables, algebraic forms and graphs of two-variable linear equations in context.
Given one quantity in a contextual linear relationship, find the other if it exists.
Write a line's equation from two points, a point and slope, or a point and a parallel or perpendicular line.

topics.title: Systems of two linear equations in two variables

outcomes.text: Create and use a system of two linear equations in two variables to solve problems in many contexts.
Identify or build a system of linear equations modelling constraints on two quantities.
Solve a system of two linear equations, using algebraic structure strategically.
Tell when a linear system has no, one or infinitely many solutions.
Connect algebraic and graphical forms of a linear system, with and without context.
Solve linear systems in two variables fluently.

topics.title: Linear inequalities in one or two variables

outcomes.text: Create and use linear inequalities in one or two variables to solve problems in many contexts.
Identify or build linear inequalities modelling constraints or conditions.
Interpret a constant, variable, factor, term or solution of a linear inequality in context.
Interpret a point in the xy-plane in terms of the solution set of an inequality or system of inequalities.
Move between tabular, algebraic and graphical forms of linear inequalities.
Factor polynomials: common factors, differences of two squares, trinomials into two binomials.
Rewrite simple rational expressions and expressions with rational exponents in radical form, and factor other polynomials.
Add, subtract and multiply polynomials fluently.

topics.title: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables

outcomes.text: Solve quadratic equations in one variable given in many forms.
Solve linear absolute value equations and simple rational and radical equations in one variable.
Solve polynomial equations in one variable written in factored form.
Solve systems of linear and nonlinear equations in two variables.
Decide when a quadratic equation has no, one or two real solutions.
Relate the solutions of a linear-nonlinear system to the graphs of its equations.
Treat a multi-variable formula as an equation in one variable of interest and solve for it.
Solve standard-form quadratics fluently, using the quadratic formula or completing the square when efficient.
Create and use quadratic or exponential functions to solve problems in many contexts.
Identify or build a quadratic or exponential function modelling a relationship.
Interpret an input/output pair, intercept, initial value, constant, variable, factor or term of a contextual quadratic or exponential function.
Interpret a point or other parts of the graph of a contextual quadratic or exponential function.
Connect table, algebraic form and graph of an untransformed quadratic or exponential function outside context.
Connect table, algebraic form and graph of polynomial, simple rational or transformed functions outside context.
Connect table, algebraic form and graph of an untransformed quadratic or exponential function in context.
Connect table, algebraic form and graph of polynomial, rational, other nonlinear or transformed functions in context.
Choose the most suitable expression form of a quadratic function to show its key features.
Choose the most suitable expression form of an exponential function to show its key features.
Use the fact that f(x)=0 gives x-intercepts and f(0) gives the y-intercept, and interpret this in context.
Evaluate a nonlinear function for an input, or find the input for a quadratic's output, using function notation.
Find the input for a given output of exponential, polynomial, radical and rational functions.

topics.title: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units

outcomes.text: Solve problems with proportional relationships, ratios and rates in many contexts, including scale drawings.
Solve problems with derived units from products (kilowatt-hours) and quotients (people per square km).
Use the fact that when one proportional quantity scales, the other scales by the same factor.
Solve problems needing a one-step unit conversion.
Solve problems needing a multistep or multidimensional unit conversion.
Use percentages in contexts such as discounts, interest, taxes and tips.
Solve percent increase and decrease problems.
Relate percent change to growth factor (5% and 1.05), including percentages of 100% or more.

topics.title: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread

outcomes.text: Interpret numerical data shown in frequency tables, histograms, dot plots and box plots.
Calculate, compare and interpret mean, median and range.
Compare distributions using center and spread, including different means or standard deviations.
Describe how outliers affect mean and median.
Interpret data in a scatterplot without making predictions.
Use a scatterplot to make predictions.
Fit linear models to scatterplot data.
Fit quadratic and exponential models to scatterplot data.
Read and interpret graphs modelling a relationship between two quantities.
Compare linear and exponential growth.
Use one- and two-way tables, area models and other displays to find relative frequency, probability and conditional probability.
Calculate, express or interpret the probability or conditional probability of an event from a display or description.
Given a probability, find an unknown count in a display or use probability to find an event's frequency.

topics.title: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error

subtopics.title: Sample statistics and margin of error

outcomes.text: Use a sample mean or proportion to estimate the population value.
Interpret margin of error and know larger samples usually shrink it.

topics.title: Evaluating statistical claims: Observational studies and experiments

outcomes.text: Say which population results from a random sample extend to.
Decide from a study's design whether it supports a causal relationship.
Explain why random assignment supports causal conclusions in an experiment.
Understand sampling issues and why results apply only to the sampled population.
Solve problems on the area or perimeter of a figure or an object modelled by one.
Solve problems on surface area or volume of a figure or modelled object.
Know that scaling by k changes lengths by k, areas by k squared and volumes by k cubed.
Choose the right area, surface area or volume formula and calculate the value.
Use congruence and similarity of triangles to solve problems.
Decide which statements are needed to prove a relationship or satisfy a theorem.
Know that scaling by k changes lengths by k but leaves angles unchanged.
Apply the triangle angle sum theorem.
Apply the vertical angle theorem and angle relationships when a transversal cuts parallel lines.
Solve problems with the Pythagorean theorem.
Use properties of special right triangles.
Solve problems with right triangle trigonometry.
Use similarity to compute sine, cosine and tangent values.
Use the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles.
Use circle definitions and theorems on radii, diameters, tangents, angles, arc lengths and sector areas.
Solve problems using radian measure or unit-circle trigonometric ratios.
Convert between degrees and radians.
Write an equation for a circle in the xy-plane.
Describe how changing a circle's equation changes its graph, and the reverse.
Understand that points satisfying (x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2 form a circle.
Complete the square in a circle equation to find its properties, and use the distance formula.
